correctness.rationale: Reconstructed graph definitions (Shrikhande Cayley steps and rook equal-coordinate adjacency), ordinary disconnected-four-set facets and dual L=all subsets whose four-subsets are connected. Independent full 2^16-mask enumeration verifies dual f-vectors S (16,120,560,668,288,0) and rook (16,120,560,620,288,48), with connected 4-set counts 668/620 and mod-2 homology dual degrees S (65,2,12), rook (96,21). The actual evidence/verify.py source constructs acyclic Morse matchings, checks every oriented Hasse incidence, signed gradient-path Morse boundaries and integral unimodular unit-pivot reductions (nonzero ranks 4,6 for S and zero for rook); these are needed to exclude torsion, which independent mod-2 checks alone cannot do. Integral Alexander duality on 16 vertices shifts L^cohomology degree 13-i and UCT applies as integral groups are free. Nonzero lower-dimensional homology obstructs shellability of pure 11-complexes. This is a complete finite graph calculation, not an assertion about all strongly regular graphs.

value.rationale: Exact torsion-sensitive homology of two canonical strongly regular parameter twins is a natural finite but complete topological invariant. The degree-nine Shrikhande class distinguishes the four-cut constructions despite equal reduced Euler characteristic; confirms nonshellability and reveals graded structure rather than a routine sampled statistic.

final_claim: Ordinary four-cut complexes of the sixteen-vertex Shrikhande and K4-square-K4 rook graphs have distinct torsion-free integral reduced homology: S has Z^12 in degree 9, Z^2 in degree 10, Z^65 in degree 11; rook has Z^21 in degree 10, Z^96 in degree 11. Both are pure dimension 11 and nonshellable.
